one_liner: Communications APIs (SMS, Messages, Voice, Video, Verify, Numbers) with self-serve API key/secret or JWT auth and free trial credit; official docs and tooling MCP servers.
notes: auth: API key+secret (sent as HTTP Basic username/password or as request params) = api_key; JWTs signed with an application private key, and HMAC message signatures (SIGNATURE_SECRET) = other. SIP Trunking digest auth also uses API key/secret (still api_key). Not included: the Vonage Network APIs (CAMARA Number Verification etc.) use an OIDC/OAuth2 authorization-code flow for end-user/operator consent (developer.vonage.com/en/api/camara/auth); that is carrier consent for a niche product line, not a way to grant a third-party app access to a Vonage account, so oauth2 was not added - a strict 'every method' reading could add it. Vonage Business Communications (UC) API is a separate product with its own token flow, excluded. access: new accounts get EUR 2 free test credit in DEMO mode (max 10 destination numbers), not time-limited -> self_serve_free; continued use is pay-as-you-go top-ups. mcp: Vonage documents two first-party MCP servers - hosted Documentation MCP (https://documentation-mcp.vonage.dev/mcp) and the Tooling / Server API Bindings MCP (npm @vonage/vonage-mcp-server-api-bindings, configured with VONAGE_API_KEY/SECRET + application private key); GitHub org Vonage has vonage-mcp-server-documentation.
